lines.title: hook
lines.text: It is three in the morning and your phone will not stop. Twenty-two alerts, one for every overheating rack. But look at the floor map: those racks are touching. This is not twenty-two problems. So how many is it?

lines.title: first incident
lines.text: Every warm cell is a rack over its temperature limit. Scan the map row by row. The first hot cell you meet starts an incident. Then flood outward: any hot cell that touches the incident, above, below, left or right, joins it. Four racks in the corner, one incident.

lines.title: claimed cells
lines.text: Keep scanning. The next hot cell that nobody has claimed starts incident two, and the flood repeats. Then a third. A claimed cell is skipped, so nothing is counted twice. Mark a cell as claimed the moment you queue it, not when you pop it, or the same rack can be queued twice.

lines.title: the rest
lines.text: Three more regions appear. Notice that no cell is ever examined more than once, so the work grows with the size of the map, not with the number of incidents.

lines.title: result
lines.text: Twenty-two hot racks collapse into six regions. Six things a person can act on instead of twenty-two pages.

lines.title: facts
lines.text: Twenty-two hot racks. Six connected regions. One visit per cell. The same flood fill powers a paint bucket, counts cells on a microscope slide, and finds lakes on a satellite image.
